questions.q: A particle is projected with velocity $u$ so that its horizontal range is three times the maximum height attained by it. The horizontal range of the projectile is given as $\frac{n u^2}{25 g}$, where value of $n$ is : (Given ' $g$ ' is the acceleration due to gravity).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Range }=3 \mathrm{H}_{\max } \\ & \frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin 2 \theta}{\mathrm{~g}}=\frac{3 \mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \mathrm{~g}}\end{aligned}$
$2 \sin \theta \cos \theta=\frac{3}{2} \sin ^2 \theta$
$\tan \theta=\frac{4}{3} \Rightarrow \theta=53^{\circ}$
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2\left(2 \times \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{4}{5}\right)}{\mathrm{g}} \Rightarrow \frac{24 \mathrm{u}^2}{25 \mathrm{~g}}$

questions.q: A particle is moving along a circular path with a constant speed of $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. What is the magnitude of the change in velocity of the particle, when it moves through an angle of $60^{\circ}$ around the centre of the circle?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Change in velocity,

\begin{array}{l}
|\Delta \overline{\mathrm{v}}|=\sqrt{\mathrm{v}_{1}^{2}+\mathrm{v}_{2}^{2}+2 \mathrm{v}_{1} \mathrm{v}_{2} \cos (\pi-\theta)} \\
=2 \mathrm{v} \sin \frac{\theta}{2} \quad\left(\because\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_{1}\right|=\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_{2}\right|\right)=\mathrm{v} \\
=(2 \times 10) \times \sin \left(30^{\circ}\right)=2 \times 10 \times \frac{1}{2} \\
=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{array}

The given data is 

θ1=30°θ2=60°u1=u2

Therefore,

H1maxH2max=u12sin2θ1u22sin2θ2=sin30°sin60°2=12322=13

questions.q: A man carrying a monkey on his shoulder does cycling smoothly on a circular track of radius $9 \mathrm{~m}$ and completes 120 resolutions in 3 minutes. The magnitude of centripetal acceleration of monkey is $\left(\right.$ in $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ) :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given : } \mathrm{R}=9 \mathrm{~m}, \\ & 120 \text { revolution in } 3 \mathrm{~min} \\ & \omega=\frac{120 \mathrm{Rev} .}{3 \mathrm{~min} .}=\frac{120 \times 2 \pi \mathrm{rad}}{3 \times 60 \mathrm{sec}}=\frac{4 \pi}{3} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \mathrm{a}_{\text {centripetal }}=\omega^2 \mathrm{R}=\left(\frac{4 \pi}{3}\right)^2 \times 9=16 \pi^2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A boy reaches the airport and finds that the escalator is not working. He walks up the stationary escalator in time t1. If he remains stationary on a moving escalator then the escalator takes him up in time t2. The time taken by him to walk up on the moving escalator will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
L= Length of escalator

Vb/ecc=Lt1

When only escalator is moving, 

Vesc=Lt2

when both are moving, 

Vb/g=Vb/esc+Vesc

Vb/g=Lt1+Lt2⇒t=LVb/g=t1t2t1+t2

questions.q: Two projectiles are fired from ground with same initial speeds from same point at angles $\left(45^{\circ}+\alpha\right)$ and $\left(45^{\circ}-\alpha\right)$ with horizontal direction. The ratio of their times of flights is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\theta_1=45+\alpha ; \theta_2=45-\alpha$
Time of flight, $\mathrm{T}=\frac{2 \mathrm{v} \sin \theta}{\mathrm{g}}$
$\frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{\sin (45+\alpha)}{\sin (45-\alpha)}$
$\frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \alpha+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \alpha}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \alpha-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \alpha}$
$\frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}=\frac{\cos \alpha+\sin \alpha}{\cos \alpha-\sin \alpha}=\frac{1+\tan \alpha}{1-\tan \alpha}$

questions.q: A stone of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi>kg</mi></math> is tied to end of a massless string of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. If the breaking tension of the string is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>, then maximum linear velocity, the stone can have without breaking the string, while rotating in horizontal plane, is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In horizontal circle, tension towards the centre of the circular path at any moment will provide the required centripetal force.

Therefore,

Tmax=mv2r⇒400=1×v21⇒v=20 m s-1

$5 \sqrt{17} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, making an angle of $\tan ^{-1} 4$ with - ve $Y$ axis

$\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}=5 t^2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{j}} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=10 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{j}} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=20 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{j}} \quad \text { at } \mathrm{t}=2 \mathrm{sec}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \tan \theta=\frac{20}{5}=4 \\ & \theta=\tan ^{-1} 4 \\ & \text { From -veY-axis }\end{aligned}$

The centripetal force acting on the vehicle is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The centripetal force is given by 

F=Mv2R=MRω2

The given data is 

M=200 kgR=70 mω=0.2 rad s-1

The magnitude of the force is 

F=200×70×0.22 N

⇒F=560 N

The kinetic energy of this ball at the highest point of its flight will become :

E=12mu2

At the Highest point, velocity is equal to the horizontal component of the velocity of projection. Therefore,

v=ucos60°=u2

∴ Kinetic energy at the topmost point =12 mu22=E4

questions.q: A ball is spun with angular acceleration <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is in second and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, the ball has angular velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and angular position of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi></math>. The most appropriate expression for the angular position of the ball is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: α=6t2-2t

Using relation α=dωdt=6t2-2t

Integrating the above, 

∫10ωdω=∫0t6t2-2tdt

⇒ω-10=2t3-t2

Now, ω=dθdt=10+2t3-t2

∫4θdθ=∫0t10+2t3-t2dt

Integrating the above relation, 

θ-4=10t+t42-t33

Thus, angular position of the ball is θ=t42-t33+10t+4.

questions.q: A body of mass $M$ thrown horizontally with velocity $v$ from the top of the tower of height $H$ touches the ground at a distance of $100 \mathrm{~m}$ from the foot of the tower. A body of mass $2 \mathrm{M}$ thrown at a velocity $\frac{v}{2}$ from the top of the tower of height $4 \mathrm{H}$ will touch the ground at a distance of _____$\mathrm{m}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 100=v \sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{g}}} ; \quad \mathrm{x}=\frac{v}{2} \sqrt{\frac{2(4 \mathrm{H})}{\mathrm{g}}}=v \sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{g}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=100\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The speed of a swimmer is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in still water. If the swimmer makes his strokes normal to the flow of river of width <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math>, he reaches a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>750</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> down the stream on the opposite bank. The speed of the river water is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let vr be velocity of river and vm be velocity of man.

Time taken by man to cross the river of width =1000 m is t=14 h.

Now, drift x=vr×t

⇒0.750=vr×14⇒vr=3 km h-1

questions.q: A car is moving on a circular path of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>600</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> such that the magnitudes of the tangential acceleration and centripetal acceleration are equal. The time taken by the car to complete first quarter of revolution, if it is moving with an initial speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>54</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>–</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

Initial speed =54×10003600=15 m s-1

at=ac

⇒vdvdx=v2R⇒∫15vdvv=1R∫0xdx

⇒v=15exR

⇒dxdt=15exR

Distance covered in first quarter of revolution =2πR4=πR2.

Therefore,

∫0πR2e-xRdx=15∫0t0dt

⇒t0=401-e-π2

Hence, t=40.

questions.q: A body is projected from the ground at an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the horizontal. Its velocity after <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The maximum height reached by the body during its motion is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math>. (use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
After 2 s the velocity is 20 m s-1

⇒vx2+vy2=v2=400

⇒u2cos245°+usin45°-gt2=u22+u2-202=400

⇒u22+u22+400-402u=400

 ⇒u2=402u⇒u=402 m s-1

Now the maximum height of the projectile is given by,

H=u2sin2θ2g⇒H=160020×2×2=20 m

questions.q: A swimmer wants to cross a river from point A to point B. Line AB makes an angle of 30° with the flow of the river. The magnitude of the velocity of the swimmer is the same as that of the river. The angle θ with the line AB should be _______°, so that the swimmer reaches point B.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Both velocity vectors are of same magnitude therefore resultant would pass exactly midway through them θ=30°
